properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-19 from flo2 F19 GENERALISED, not as a proposal.

THE OPTIONS.
(a) NARROW THE POOL by extending the tool-to-type map until no tool is pooled into every type. Direct, and it turns 24 excused properties into a list somebody reads once. COUNTER: the map is hand-maintained, so this trades a silent false all-clear for a file that goes stale — unless the gate refuses a tool it cannot place, which is the real version of the option.
(b) RANK BY WHETHER ANYTHING READS THE PROPERTY. `Requirement.kind` is urgent because `encoding_undecided` scolds a user about it on flo2's page; `Verification.location` is documented and read by nothing. A property a DETECTOR reads and no tool can write is a promise the product breaks in front of a user, and deserves a louder bucket than an unused declaration.
(c) FIX THE TWO KNOWN CASES AND LEAVE THE GATE. Cheapest, and it is what the reporter says is worth doing regardless. COUNTER, theirs: two found by accident is weak evidence that two is the total, and this leaves the instrument still blind.
(d) DROP THE PER-TYPE VIEW and report the flat name match with its known over-reporting, on the grounds that a noisy true signal beats a quiet false one. COUNTER: that is the naive match this instrument was explicitly built to replace, and it was replaced because the noise made it unread.

⚠️ WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE TWO KNOWN CASES ARE SEPARABLE AND SMALL: a `kind` parameter on add_requirement, and a `location` on add_verification. The gate question is the one that decides whether a third case is found by a consumer or by the build.
properties.name: OPEN — should the reachability gate attach each tool's parameters only to the types that tool actually writes, and should a property a detector READS be held to a stricter bar than one nothing reads?
